name: Strety
tagline: Runs EOS-style weekly meetings, scorecards, rocks, to-dos and issue lists inside Slack and Microsoft Teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not hard: metrics with weekly targets, quarterly rocks with owners, to-dos, a prioritized issues list, and a timed agenda that walks a meeting through all of it. An agent can produce a working version of that in a sitting, and the structure of the meeting is public knowledge from a book anyone can buy. The catch is that this is a team ritual, not a personal tool: the value shows up when seven people all see the same scorecard and get nudged in the channel they already live in. Rebuilding the app is a weekend; rebuilding the Slack and Teams bot surface, the auth, and the habit of everyone actually opening it is the part that eats you. Build it if you run a small team that already lives in one place and you want the spreadsheet to stop being a spreadsheet.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted web app with a weekly scorecard grid, quarterly rocks, to-dos and an issues list, plus a timed meeting mode that walks the agenda segment by segment and saves the outcome.
requirements: A box or container to host it on so the whole team can reach the same instance
Shared login of some kind, even a crude one, since this is inherently multi-user
Someone willing to chase people about entering their numbers before the meeting
whatYouLose: Slack and Microsoft Teams bots: reminders, to-do capture and scorecard nudges where people already are
Mobile access that does not feel like a desktop site squeezed into a phone
Accountability chart, vision docs and the rest of the EOS paperwork in one place
Any kind of onboarding or coach-friendly structure when a new person joins the team
Someone else maintaining it when the meeting is in four minutes and the page is blank
moatNotes: The moat is not the schema, it is that the tool sits inside Slack and Teams where the team already argues.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the thing being sold is not a database of metrics, it is the weekly meeting actually happening the same way every week with everyone looking at the same numbers. A homegrown version works right up until two people stop updating their rows, at which point the meeting quietly reverts to a spreadsheet and then to vibes. Paying per seat creates a small, useful amount of institutional pressure, and the Slack and Teams integrations mean nobody has to remember a new URL. For a team that has committed to EOS and pays a coach to keep them honest, a few dollars a head is rounding error against that.
notes: The meeting format is from a book, not from the vendor, which is why the build is easy and the adoption is not.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted weekly team meeting app for EOS-style Level 10 meetings. Empty folder, start from scratch.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/app.db.
- Single Docker Compose service, port 3000, volume mounted at /app/data.
- Auth: one shared team password from TEAM_PASSWORD in .env, set as an httpOnly cookie. No OAuth, no accounts, no email.

Data model:
- Person: name, active flag.
- Metric: name, owner (Person), target number, comparator (gte or lte), display order.
- MetricEntry: metric, ISO week string, value.
- Rock: title, owner, quarter string, status (on-track, off-track, done).
- Todo: title, owner, due date, done flag, created week.
- Issue: title, notes, created week, priority rank, solved flag, solved week.
- Meeting: date, duration seconds, notes, rating 1 to 10.

Screens:
- /scorecard: grid of metrics as rows, last 13 ISO weeks as columns, inline editable cells, cell background green or red based on target and comparator.
- /rocks: quarterly rocks grouped by owner with a status toggle.
- /meeting: the main event. A timed agenda with these segments and default minutes: Segue 5, Scorecard 5, Rock Review 5, Headlines 5, To-Do List 5, IDS 60, Conclude 5. Show a countdown per segment and a total elapsed clock, Next and Back buttons, and render the relevant data inside each segment (scorecard grid in Scorecard, rock list in Rock Review, open todos in To-Do List, drag-sortable issues list in IDS with a Solve button). Conclude captures notes and a 1 to 10 rating and writes a Meeting row.
- /history: past meetings with ratings and notes.

Rules:
- Solved issues auto-archive, unsolved ones carry to next week.
- Todos older than two weeks and still open get flagged visually.
- Seed script creates 4 people, 6 metrics, 3 rocks and 5 issues so the UI is not empty.

Out of scope, do not build: Slack or Teams bots, email reminders, mobile apps, multi-tenant orgs, per-user permissions, analytics, telemetry, any external API call.

Ship a README with: docker compose up, the .env keys, and a one-paragraph explanation of the meeting format for anyone who has not read the book.
